scenes.dialogue: Hi, I am Ravishankar from LawWorld. A court summons arrives at Asha's home. Her neighbour says a summons means the police will arrest her.
That is wrong. A summons directs attendance. A warrant authorises arrest.
A proclamation addresses a person believed to be absconding or hiding, so that a warrant cannot be executed.
Each has its own conditions under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, and the Supreme Court insists that courts move through them in order.
Section Sixty Three describes a court summons. It is in writing, signed and sealed.
scenes.shown: Section 63 describes a court summons. It is in writing, signed and sealed.

scenes.dialogue: It may also be an encrypted electronic communication bearing the image of the court's seal, or a digital signature.
Read the court, the case, the person summoned, the purpose and the date. A summons can call an accused or a witness. It does not establish guilt.
An electronic message should be verified through official court channels.
Section Sixty Four governs service: personally where practicable, or by electronic communication in the form the State Government prescribes.
scenes.shown: Section 64 governs service: personally where practicable, or by electronic communication in the form the State Government prescribes.

scenes.dialogue: Sections Sixty Five to Seventy One cover companies, absent persons, government servants and witnesses.
scenes.shown: Sections 65 to 71 cover companies, absent persons, government servants and witnesses.

scenes.dialogue: There is no universal rule that a summons gives exactly seven or fifteen days.
scenes.shown: There is no universal rule that a summons gives exactly seven or 15 days.

scenes.dialogue: The appearance date on the document controls. Asha should preserve it, and act promptly. Refusing the envelope does not make the case disappear.
Suppose Asha is an accused, and is in hospital on the hearing date. She should place the difficulty before the court through counsel.
Section Two Twenty Eight allows a Magistrate who issues a summons to dispense with personal attendance, and permit appearance through an advocate.
scenes.shown: Section 228 allows a Magistrate who issues a summons to dispense with personal attendance, and permit appearance through an advocate.

scenes.dialogue: In Bhaskar Industries, the Supreme Court confirmed this can cover even the first appearance.
But it remains a court decision. A private message to the complainant excuses nothing.
Under Section Seventy Two, an arrest warrant is a written order signed by the presiding officer, and bearing the court's seal.
scenes.shown: Under Section 72, an arrest warrant is a written order signed by the presiding officer, and bearing the court's seal.

scenes.dialogue: It remains in force until executed, or cancelled by the issuing court. It does not expire because a hearing date has passed.
If Asha learns of a warrant, the practical response is to obtain its details, and apply to the court promptly to recall or convert it, rather than hide.
Section Seventy Three allows the court to endorse on the warrant that, if the person gives a bond with sureties, the executing officer must release them.
scenes.shown: Section 73 allows the court to endorse on the warrant that, if the person gives a bond with sureties, the executing officer must release them.

scenes.dialogue: This is commonly called a bailable warrant. A warrant without that endorsement does not mean bail can never be granted.
It means the officer cannot release on the warrant itself, so bail must be sought from the court.
The Supreme Court has cautioned against issuing non bailable warrants casually.
scenes.shown: The Supreme Court has cautioned against issuing non-bailable warrants casually.

scenes.dialogue: Section Ninety allows a court to issue a warrant instead of, or in addition to, a summons, after recording reasons in writing.
scenes.shown: Section 90 allows a court to issue a warrant instead of, or in addition to, a summons, after recording reasons in writing.
scenes.chip: 7 · WHEN A COURT MAY ISSUE A WARRANT

scenes.dialogue: That is where it has reason to believe the person has absconded, or will not obey.
Or where the person fails to appear without reasonable excuse, after a summons duly served.
The Supreme Court adds a sequence: summons first, then a bailable warrant, and a non bailable warrant only when the person is avoiding court.
scenes.shown: The Supreme Court adds a sequence: summons first, then a bailable warrant, and a non-bailable warrant only when the person is avoiding court.

scenes.dialogue: Under Section Eighty Four, the court must have reason to believe that a person against whom it has issued a warrant has absconded, or is hiding.
scenes.shown: Under Section 84, the court must have reason to believe that a person against whom it has issued a warrant has absconded, or is hiding.

scenes.dialogue: So that the warrant cannot be executed.
It may then publish a proclamation requiring appearance at a specified place and time, at least thirty days from publication.
scenes.shown: It may then publish a proclamation requiring appearance at a specified place and time, at least 30 days from publication.

scenes.dialogue: One missed hearing does not satisfy these conditions.
Ignoring a proclamation is itself an offence under Section Two Hundred Nine of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
scenes.shown: Ignoring a proclamation is itself an offence under Section 209 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

scenes.dialogue: Section Eighty Five permits attachment of property by a reasoned order after proclamation.
scenes.shown: Section 85 permits attachment of property by a reasoned order after proclamation.

scenes.dialogue: Or simultaneously, where property may be disposed of or removed. A summons alone never leads to attachment.
Under Section Eighty Four, sub section four, a person proclaimed for a grave offence who still fails to appear may, after inquiry, be declared a proclaimed offender.
scenes.shown: Under Section 84(4), a person proclaimed for a grave offence who still fails to appear may, after inquiry, be declared a proclaimed offender.

scenes.dialogue: Such a person is normally not entitled to anticipatory bail, and Section Three Fifty Six allows trial in their absence.
scenes.shown: Such a person is normally not entitled to anticipatory bail, and Section 356 allows trial in their absence.

scenes.dialogue: The safest response to court process is organised action. Verify the document. Note the appearance date.
Identify whether you are an accused or a witness, and obtain legal assistance.
If attendance is genuinely difficult, seek the court's permission before the date, not after.
A summons calls you to court. A warrant authorises arrest. A proclamation requires further findings about evasion.
Knowing the difference lets you respond without panic, or dangerous delay.
